ayahOccurrences.text: هُوَ ٱلَّذِى يُسَيِّرُكُمْ فِى ٱلْبَرِّ وَٱلْبَحْرِ ۖ حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا كُنتُمْ فِى ٱلْفُلْكِ وَجَرَيْنَ بِهِم بِرِيحٍ طَيِّبَةٍ وَفَرِحُوا۟ بِهَا جَآءَتْهَا رِيحٌ عَاصِفٌ وَجَآءَهُمُ ٱلْمَوْجُ مِن كُلِّ مَكَانٍ وَظَنُّوٓا۟ أَنَّهُمْ أُحِيطَ بِهِمْ ۙ دَعَوُا۟ ٱللَّهَ مُخْلِصِينَ لَهُ ٱلدِّينَ لَئِنْ أَنجَيْتَنَا مِنْ هَٰذِهِۦ لَنَكُونَنَّ مِنَ ٱلشَّٰكِرِينَ

lexSnapshot.derivativeNote: طَيِّبَٰتِ is in the derivative form: طَيِّب
lexSnapshot.rootDefinitionHtml:
ط/ي/ب ṭ–y–b to be good, to be agreeable, to be willing, to mollify
; to be wholesome, to become ripe; to regain health; to be fragrant, fragrance, perfume. It has been suggested by some scholars that the derivative طُوبَى ṭūbā is linked to a corresponding Syriac and a common Semitic root. Other scholars attribute the derivative طُوبَى ṭūbā to a borrowing from Hindi.

Of this root, 6 forms occur 50 times the Qur’an:
طَابَ ṭāba 3 times; طُوبَى ṭūbā 1 time; طَيِّب ṭayyib 13 times; طَيِّبُون ṭayyibūn 3 times; طَيِّبةٌ ṭayyibatun 9 times and طَيِّبات ṭayyibāt 21 times.
lexSnapshot.mainDefinitionHtml:
طَيِّب ṭayyib [quasi-act. part.; pl. طَيِّبُون ṭayyibūn; fem. طَيِّبةٌ ṭayyibatun; fem. pl. طَيِّبات ṭayyibāt]

1 good

(14:24)‏كَلِمَةً‏ ‏طَيِّبَةً‏ ‏كَشَجَرَةٍ‏ ‏طَيِّبَةٍ‏ ‏a good word is like a good tree

2 the Pious, the chaste

(24:26) ‏الطَّيِّبَاتُ‏ ‏لِلطَّيِّبِينَ‏ ‏وَالطَّيِّبُونَ‏ ‏لِلطَّيِّبَاتِ‏ the chaste women are for the chaste men, and the chaste men are for the chaste women

3 clean

(4:43) ‏فَتَيَمَّمُوا‏ ‏صَعِيدًا‏ ‏طَيِّبًا‏‏ then select clean earth

4 wholesome

(16:114) فَكُلُوا مِمَّا رَزَقَكُمُ اللَّهُ حَلاَلا طَيِّبًا so eat of the wholesome and lawful things God has provided for you

5 favourable, fair

(10:22) حَتَّى إِذَا كُنْتُمْ فِى الْفُلْكِ وَجَرَيْنَ بِهِمْ بِرِيحٍ طَيِّبَةٍ till when you are in the ships and they sail with them [you] on a fair wind

6 agreeable, pleasant

(61:12)‏‏ُوَمَسَاكِنَ‏ ‏طَيِّبَةً‏ ‏فِى‏ ‏جَنَّاتِ‏ ‏عَدْنٍ‏‏ into pleasant dwellings in the Gardens of Eternity.

entries.label: طَابَ
entries.definitionHtml:
طَابَ ṭāba ı [v. intrans.]

1 to be or become desirable or agreeable

(4:3) ‏فَانْكِحُوا‏ ‏مَا‏ ‏طَابَ‏ ‏لَكُمْ‏ ‏مِنَ‏ ‏النِّسَاءِ‏ ‏ then marry of [the other] women those who seem agreeable to you

2 to become good, to be good, to become pious, to be pious

(39:73) وَقَالَ لَهُمْ خَزَنَتُهَا سَلاَمٌ عَلَيْكُمْ طِبْتُمْ فَادْخُلُوهَا خَالِدِينَ ‏and its keepers say to them, ‘Peace be upon you, you have been good, enter it, [to dwell] for ever’; *

(4:4) فَإِنْ طِبْنَ لَكُمْ عَنْ شَيْءٍ مِنْهُ نَفْسًا‏ but if they are, of their own accord, happy to give up some of it for you.

entries.label: طُوبَى
entries.definitionHtml:
طُوبَى ṭūbā [v. n./n.] variously interpreted as: the name of a tree in Paradise, borrowing from Ethiopian or Hindi meaning paradise, borrowing from Persian meaning golden, or noun meaning happiness, joy, goodness or affluence

(13:29) الَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ الصَّالِحَاتِ طُوبَى لَهُمْ وَحُسْنُ مَآبٍ those who believe and do righteous deeds, joy is theirs and for them an excellent homecoming.
